plan: Given my low private value of $2, my strategy is to bid conservatively to avoid a loss. I expect the other bidders to bid closer to their values, likely higher than mine. By bidding a small amount, I minimize potential losses if I unexpectedly win. The optimal bid is slightly above the lowest likely bid to avoid paying more than my value. I will bid $0.5, hoping the other bids are significantly higher, ensuring I don't win and incur a loss.

Given my value of $11, I aim to bid just below my value to ensure potential profit while minimizing loss. Assuming other bids are uniformly distributed, they may average around $24.5. I will bid $10.9 to win only if others bid lower. If I win, I pay the third-highest bid, maximizing profit. If others bid higher, I lose nothing. This strategy balances risk and reward, optimizing long-term profit.

Given my private value of $14, I aim to bid slightly above half my value to maximize potential profit while minimizing loss. Assuming Andy and Betty bid near their values, bidding around $7.5 might win if their values are below mine. If they bid higher, I lose nothing. If I win, paying the third-highest bid should yield profit, as it's likely lower than my value. This strategy balances winning chances and profit maximization.
